reading.body:
The only thing this record establishes is that someone tagged a point in Italy as a data center. It records no capacity, no operator, and no confirmation.

The tag is telecom=data_center on an OpenStreetMap node named iZOOM.it, at coordinates in northern Italy whose nearest listed airport is Parma, 18.7 miles away. The name carries a .it suffix, a naming pattern common among Italian web-hosting and domain-registration businesses. The record's own research note reads it as plausibly a small hosting or IT services operation, not as a confirmed large facility. The capacity field is zero, which in a record this thin reads as unrecorded rather than as a measured zero.

For AI scaling, that distinction is the whole point. Compute buildout is counted in megawatts and operators, and this record supplies neither. A hosting company's server room and a hyperscale campus can both attract the same tag, so the tag alone cannot be used to size anything. Anyone assembling a map of Italian data center capacity from records like this one would be counting labels, not load.

What the data does not cover is nearly everything. Scale, service offering, and current operating status are all unconfirmed, and the research stopped because the search quota ran out, so the absence of confirmation is not evidence that the business is small or inactive. City and state fields are empty, leaving coordinates as the only locational anchor. One node is not a census, and it says nothing about Italy's data center capacity as a whole.
